direct_answer: Foot and ankle osteoarthritis can make walking painful and less steady. Supportive footwear, insoles, clear routes, good lighting and suitable walking aids can help you walk indoors more safely. A podiatrist or physiotherapist can advise.
author: Louis Maxwell

content:
Painful feet change how you walk and can increase falls risk.

This guide covers safer indoor walking. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Footwear

  • Supportive, cushioned shoes with a firm heel.
  • Avoid loose slippers.
  • Velcro fastenings if hands are sore.

Home routes

  • Clear clutter and trailing wires.
  • Good lighting, including at night.
  • Furniture or rails to steady you.

Getting help

A podiatrist can advise on insoles and footwear. A physiotherapist can help with strength and balance.

Midfoot pain and standing

  • Supportive, cushioned shoes indoors can help more than slippers.
  • Sit for tasks such as preparing food.
  • A podiatrist may suggest insoles or a stiffer-soled shoe.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Are slippers OK?

Well-fitting, supportive ones are safer.

How do I see a podiatrist?

Ask your GP; some areas allow self-referral.
